As we discussed on a call, Privacy Team does not have concerns on the Courier Selfie-Check.*To reiterate the agreed setup:*

* Couriers should be asked consent *before* they provide their selfie for the check ([+as for drivers+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/3871768748/Driver+Selfie+Verification]). This consent is about conducting the automated facial recognition (extracting and comparing facial measurements by a machine).
* If the courier does not agree on the automated check, we need to have a human manual review of the selfies and comparison with the IDs or other documents ([+the same as for drivers+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/3871768748/Driver+Selfie+Verification]).
** To note, if the courier rejects, we should not allow him to go online, we just need to opt for the manual review by Ops
** This rejection of consent does not apply to metadata checks, eg selfie can be used for metadata check by a machine, but the face match, detection and selfie liveliness should be conducted manually only.
* As agreed, if we see a spike in courier's complaints that they submit selfie multiple times with a good quality or fixing other issues, but the system still rejects, we need to step in and check what the issue is (on the Verification team side).

However, I have one related, yet a bit different question to ask: I assume we can have ordinary termination w/o any reason if we give them another 30 days to deliver, right?

I’m thinking about cases where couriers get blocked every single week (for now we only noticed that with low AR, as we did not have any blockings for 0% AR so far). As we usually conduct courier low AR blockings on Monday, all blocked couriers can go back online on Friday evening/Saturday. For some of them that might be the only days they work, so current blocking we have does not really impact their regular delivering schedule. 

I want to have a monthy/quarterly checkup when we terminate contracts with all couriers who continue to get blocked (does not improve their quality). Best case scenario would be that we *don’t need any warning comms* and check on their progress (give them an additional chance to improve after warnings are sent).

I’m sharing how I’d see an ideal process from my team perspective (least time consuming):

*Every month* we check frequency of current AR blockings. If courier got blocked 6 times out of possible 12 (which would be every week of the quarter) in the last 3 months, we terminate contract with him. Even if courier is active with us only for 2 months (not even for 3 months), but already has 6 low AR blockings during that period, we could terminate his contract immediatelly.

I’m prefering immediate termination because of two reasons:

# Main reason: this would make process easier. We would not ned to send any additional warning comms and collect data about who has already received warning email from us and who has not.
# Less important, but still valid reason: We can take action as soon as we notice courier constantly providing poor performance and we do not need to let our quality suffer for another 30 days.

I can create a separate ticket if that would be more convenient.

Thanks for your help in advance! 💚

To share driver leads and active driver data with the fleet, we need to take the following steps to ensure GDPR compliance:

# *Obtain consent:*
#* We can’t rely on the existing Terms and Conditions for this data transfer because they don’t cover sharing data with a new legal entity.
#* We need to inform drivers about the transfer, explain why their data will be shared, and get their explicit consent. This should include:
#** Who the joint venture is and its role.
#** The purpose of contacting drivers (e.g., helping them create their own fleet).
#** Assurance that their data will only be used for this purpose and will be protected.
#** A clear opt-in mechanism, allowing drivers to actively agree to the data transfer.
# *Data Sharing Agreement:*
#* We need to establish a Data Sharing Agreement between Bolt and the joint venture. This should define:
#** Each party’s roles and responsibilities.
#** Security measures to protect the shared data.
#** How to handle data subject requests (e.g., access or deletion requests).
#* I’ll draft this agreement tailored to this joint venture’s specific situation.
# *Transparency:*
#* We need to send a communication to all affected drivers, ensuring they are informed and giving them the option to consent.
# *Next Steps:*

*_Deposit auto-charge duration_*

_Hey_ [_@thiago.delbel_|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U031X5KJSTV]_, to give you some quick context: regarding deposits, we need to set the number of days between issuing the fine and automatically charging the deposit. We can't use the 14 day period we normally use, because we will likely lose the deposit much sooner (e.g. in 3-5 days from issuing the fine). Are we tied here to something in the T&C? Or can we set this period to be shorter; something like 3 days, for example?_

[_@pavel.nekrasov_|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U01G3ATPT0V] _for reference, what is the current logic in station-based?_

_Thiago Del Bel_  [_Just now_|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C08928Z00FN/p1740650716492559?thread_ts=1740647431.613839&cid=C08928Z00FN]
_Hey_ [_@ahmed.elagha_|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U053ZJ9U31A]_, we can set a shorter period. Would the logic be similar to “non-deposit charges”? As in, we communicate the charge to the user, allow 3 days (for example) for consenting or disputing it, and if there’s consent or the 3 days elapse, we charge the deposit. What if the user objects?_

_Quickly explaining the rationale for the 14 days for “non-deposit charges”.  In this case, Bolt automatically charges the user’s in-App payment method, which the user cannot reasonably expect without prior communication. When users link a payment method to the Bolt App they don’t authorise Bolt to charge whatever amounts Bolt finds due without prior communication, opportunity to dispute etc._

_With the deposit, Bolt previously communicates to users that the amount is intended to cover penalties, damages etc. occurring during the ride. The user accepts this condition before renting the vehicle and, therefore, should not be surprised by a subsequent charge, provided that it’s duly substantiated._

I checked the other queries and it looks we have one which queries by status='queued', implying that we need a status index, and taking into consideration only recent entities may be queued, it make sense to have this index as the majority of entries have the status equals ‘done' or 'unsupported’.

Adding two indexes one for {{external_entity_id}} and one for {{status}} implies a bit slower write performance (writing into two indexes is slower than writing into one composite index for status, {{external_entity_id}}). By having just one index implies we always need to add the status in our queries in order to benefit from it. As we are not having any write issues right now, it worths having 2 separate indexes, and avoid adding redundant things into WHERE clauses.

{noformat}SELECT
                    du.id,
                    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.created) as created,
                    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.last_update) as last_update,
                    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.start_processing_after) as start_processing_after,
                    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.processed_at) as processed_at,
                    du.status,

                FROM ${TableNames.documentUnit} du

	d.created,
	d.meta.city_id,
	CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.search_category_id') AS bigint) AS search_category,
	CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.order.order_id') AS bigint) AS order_id,
	CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.paid_wait_fee')AS double) AS paid_wait_local,
	CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.paid_wait_fee')AS double)/r.rate AS paid_wait_eur,
	CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.features.number_destination_changes')AS int) AS dest_changes,
	CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.features.number_stops')AS int) AS stops,
	json_array_length(json_extract(d.input, '$.data.stops')) AS count_inputs,
	COALESCE((CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.driver_timestamp.driving_with_client') AS double)-CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.driver_timestamp.arrived_to_client')AS double)),0) AS pickup_wait_time,
	COALESCE((CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.stops.2.timestamp') AS bigint) - CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.stops.1.timestamp') AS bigint)),0) AS wait_time_1_stop,
	COALESCE((CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.stops.4.timestamp') AS bigint) - CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.stops.3.timestamp') AS bigint)),0) AS wait_time_2_stop,
	COALESCE((CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.stops.2.timestamp') AS bigint) - CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.stops.1.timestamp') AS bigint)),0)+COALESCE((CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.stops.4.timestamp') AS bigint) - CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.stops.3.timestamp') AS bigint)),0) AS total_wait_time_stops,
	s.actions,
	d.decision.decision
	FROM archive_analytical.driver_overcharge_check d
	CROSS JOIN UNNEST (d.decision.actions) AS s(actions)
	JOIN 
		(
		SELECT
			pcc.search_category_id, 
			pcc.name,
			pcc.value
			FROM ng_public.pricing_config_configuration pcc
			WHERE 
			pcc.name LIKE 'is_paid_stops_enabled'
			AND value = 'true'
		) AS config ON CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.search_category_id') AS bigint) = config.search_category_id
	LEFT JOIN ng_public.currency_exchange_rates r ON json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.order.currency') = r.currency AND DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(d.created) - INTERVAL '1' DAY
	WHERE d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
	AND s.actions = 'remove_paid_wait_time'
) AS y
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC
--LIMIT 200{noformat}

Hi [~accountid:62136b1b2d057500723e36ba] Apologies for the long wait here!

There are couple of questions we would need to evaluate before we can proceed with this feature.

Firstly, as a summary, *Offline trips* - a feature which allows making rides without rider account creation. Drivers can create a ride after picking a payment method (cash or terminal, no in-app payments available) and destination. Basically, in this case Bolt App serves as a taximeter to calculate the price and trip details. There is no relationship created between Bolt and the rider, that is picked up just from the street

Aspects that need to be considered before enabling this:

* data protection - what rider data is supposed to be collected and processed;
* safety - if we do not collect rider data, we know nothing about the rider and therefore, we are unable to ensure driver and rider safety;
* some in-app features might not work properly due to a lack of a rider account that booked a trip;
* local operating entity may still be exposed to end-user liability even though the rider does not have a rider account and contractual relationship with Bolt.

Thus I’m involving to the ticket also our Safety, Privacy and Product Legal teams. 

Once the feature is green lighted by everyone, we will be needing to also make adjustments to our T&Cs.

h3. *1. Summary of the Processing Activity*

Bolt plans to implement a *risk-based deposit system* for Bolt Drive. This system analyses user data (e.g., driving history, fines, time of rental, country of residence, age, driving experience) to determine *whether a deposit is required and its amount*. The goal is to *reduce financial risk* while minimising the impact on low-risk users.

h3. *2. Article 22 GDPR Applies*

Since the deposit amount is *determined by an automated system*, prohibition of automated decision-making ([Article 22 GDPR|https://gdpr-info.eu/art-22-gdpr/]) may apply if the decision has *a legal or similarly significant effect* on users. If the deposit is so high that it *effectively prevents certain users from renting*, this could be considered a significant impact under GDPR.

h3. *3. Overview of Available Legal Bases*

* *Legitimate Interest (Art. 6(1)(f))* → Best fit, as Bolt has a valid business need to mitigate financial risk.
* *Contractual Necessity (Art. 6(1)(b))* → Unlikely to apply, as a deposit is a *risk mitigation measure*, not essential for performing the contract.
* *Consent (Art. 6(1)(a))* → Could be used but is impractical, as requiring consent for risk-based deposits may reduce effectiveness.

h3. *4. Argument for "No Significant Effect"*

A deposit may *not* be considered a "significant effect" under Article 22 if:

* *It is a temporary hold, not a permanent charge* - users do not lose money unless they incur fines/damages.
* *Users can still rent the car* - the deposit does not deny service outright.
* *Refunds are processed quickly* - reducing financial burden.
* *Alternatives are available* - such as lower deposits for good drivers, insurance waivers, or instalment payments.
* *Users can challenge high deposits* - offering *human review* ensures fairness and weakens the claim that the decision is purely automated.

h3. *5. Alternative Option*

If regulators determine that the deposit *does* have a significant effect, Bolt must:
➡ *Obtain explicit consent (Art. 6(1)(a))*, OR
➡ *Ensure human review* is available so that users can contest deposit decisions and request manual adjustments.

h3. 6. Data Minimisation & Proportionality (Art. 5(1)(c)) 

The initiative must ensure only necessary data is processed. Some high-risk data points include: 

* Fraud score signals - If derived from external sources, this requires strong justification. 
* Country of residence & DL country - indirect discrimination concerns?
* Time of day & day of week - Needs clear justification that such factors correlate with risk. 

Alternative, less intrusive methods should be considered, such as *using only historical ride and fine data* instead of broader personal identifiers.

“affiliate” in the NDA is defined broadly to ensure that any entity within either party’s corporate group is bound by the same confidentiality obligations. Thank you for sharing that Winbond has no affiliates involved, however this provision remains relevant for Bolt, as we have multiple group entities (e.g., Bolt Operations, Bolt Technology, and various local subsidiaries) that may need to access, share or handle confidential information.

Given that Winbond does not have affiliates, this clause is unlikely to impose additional obligations or risks for Winbond, but it ensures that Bolt’s confidentiality protections remain intact now and if Winbond’s group or the contemplated transaction evolves or changes. Removing the definition could create ambiguity or gaps in confidentiality coverage, particularly if any entity within the Bolt group is required to receive, share or process confidential information. 

We propose to keep the clause as drafted. If there are additional concerns, please share.

country = ke
predicted duration between 650 and 1250
predicted distance between 6000 and 7100
distance 5x larger than prediction
duration 1.8x larger than prediction
trip start/end location distance between 3.5km and 4.5km



{code:sql}select do.created,
do.id,
CONCAT ('https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/calculations/driver_order_finish/', CAST(do.id AS varchar)) as calc_link,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.data.order_id') AS order_id,
CONCAT ('https://kenya-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/', CAST(json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.data.order_id') AS varchar)) as order_link,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.data.country') AS country,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.data.city_id') as city_id,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.driver_arrived_to_client_lat') as driver_arrived_to_client_lat,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.driver_arrived_to_client_lng') as driver_arrived_to_client_lng,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.driving_with_client_lat') as driving_with_client_lat,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.driving_with_client_lng') as driving_with_client_lng,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.arrived_to_destination_lat') as arrived_to_destination_lat,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.arrived_to_destination_lng') as arrived_to_destination_lng,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.prediction_data.distance') as predicted_distance,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.ride_distance') as ride_distance,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.prediction_data.duration') as predicted_duration,
json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.ride_duration') as ride_duration,
ROUND(great_circle_distance(
cast(json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.driving_with_client_lat') as DOUBLE PRECISION),
cast(json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.driving_with_client_lng') as DOUBLE PRECISION),

cast(json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.driving_with_client_lng') as DOUBLE PRECISION),
cast(json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.order.arrived_to_destination_lat') as DOUBLE PRECISION),

--
and cast(json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.prediction_data.duration') as decimal) between 650 and 1250
and cast(json_extract_scalar(do."INPUT",'$.additional.prediction_data.distance') as decimal) between 6000 and 7100

All taxi and ride-hailing drivers in Lithuania are required to hold increased-risk third-party motor vehicle liability (MTPL) insurance. MTPL insurance compensates for damages to third-party property and/or health, as well as non-pecuniary damages, when the damage occurs due to the fault of the motor vehicle owner or possessor. Thus, MTPL covers cases where passengers suffer bodily injuries.

If a driver is unable to present increased-risk MTPL insurance to the LTSA, the LTSA must refuse to renew or issue a new license. Therefore, the ultimate responsibility for ensuring that only eligible individuals are issued a license rests with the LTSA.

Please note that the LTSA does not disclose its internal processes regarding the frequency of driver license checks and suspensions. However, considering that the requirement to obtain increased-risk MTPL insurance took effect only on May 1, 2024, and that any driver who failed to apply for license renewal with the required insurance by December 20, 2024, had their license automatically expire on January 1, 2025, all drivers recently underwent scrutiny by the LTSA.

Additionally, all drivers were required to submit their renewed licenses to Bolt at the end of 2024 or the beginning of 2025. Therefore, we can confirm that all drivers currently active on the Bolt platform hold a valid license and valid MTPL insurance.
______
Regarding their request to add a clause stating that if the driver’s insurance does not cover third-party injuries, Bolt will undertake the coverage—I do not want to include such a clause. This is not our responsibility, nor is it our obligation to verify the insurance. Is there any way we can push back on this?

If, from a business perspective, you believe this client is valuable enough to justify adding the clause, we can consider it. However, it is excessive for us as a platform operator to take on such obligations, and I do not want to set a precedent for other clients.

[~accountid:5eb363355862510b794e3507] when adjusting the disc brake, it is important to set the static (inner) pad as close to the rotor as possible. Set it so that it slightly drags and then one notch back.

Then set up the outer pad/cable so that the brake works as desired. If the inner pad is not very close to the rotor, the rotor has to bend towards the static pad and the brake feels mushy and braking performance is poor.



Some manuals on the internet state that the gap should be equal, but I think that is suggested to decrease the risk of people accidentally flipping over the bars if the brakes are too powerful/grabby. With our brakes it will not be an issue, small rotor and not that powerful brakes to begin with. We can fine tune it later, if it turns out to be a problem, but in this test we want best performance.

I made a picture to explan.

Also, this kind of setup lets the static pad wear more before it needs adjustment again.

*Instructions for Tier 1 agents*

h4. *I want to register for the Branding program*

*I didn’t receive a branding enrollment message, I want to report a car branding being damaged or they want to remove the sticker* 

The partner needs to send a picture of the damage sticker:

* If the partner sends the picture and it is true, escalate this to Local Ops Tier in Beehive, specifying that the damage has been validated
* If not, escalate this to Local Ops Tier in Beehive, specifying what happened too 

* Inform the user that we'll forward their request



h4. *I didn't receive my branding bonus* 

* Check by the FO Admin Id or email if any Compensation related to Branding is visible, depending on the month or week the branding bonus should be added. Go to, Admin Panel > Rides > Fleet > Companies > Balance > Balance history > Balance Movements [ |https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/balance?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22start_date_ts%22%3A1739919600%2C%22end_date_ts%22%3A1740005999%2C%22types%22%3A%5B%22ride_hailing_fleet%22%5D%2C%22external_id%22%3A116554%2C%22namespace%22%3A%22_empty_%22%7D%7D]| Balance Guide > Filter by dates > click on External id to see the Type of Compensation. A compensation related to Branding is added as ‘Compensation’ with an amount higher than 100€. Make sure the compensation isn’t related to a trip.
* If the compensation is reflected, inform the FO and _Solved_ the case.
* If a compensation isn’t reflected, and is from the previous month or previous week, advise the FO to check if the conditions were met. * If it is from the current week, tell the FO to wait for the coming payout, and if it isn't reflected check if the conditions were met, you can share the Manual. If these were met, but he didn’t get the bonus, he can contact us again by sending us a screenshot of the conditions. _Solved_ the case.

# 🚗 [Rider: My driver refused to make a requested stop|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013967299?country=global&language=en] - for cases when the rider’s *requested stop was skipped* (and the trip was completed from pickup to destination, but excluding the additional stop). 

For the 1st case, the process instructs agents to consider if 50% of the trip was finished and either give a full refund or a goodwill compensation, so it’s fair to the customers. {noformat}SELECT 
y.unblock_group,
y.country,
--CASE WHEN y.unblock_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_unblocked_after,
--approx_distinct(y.country,0.0041) AS count_distinct_countries,
--array_agg(y.country) AS countries_list,
approx_distinct(y.unblock_id, 0.0041) count_distinct_unblocks
--approx_distinct(y.id,0.0041) AS count_distinct_blocks
--approx_distinct(y.driver_id, 0.0041) count_drivers_unblocked
FROM (
 SELECT
da.driver_id AS driver_id,
fdr.id AS driver_root_id,
CONCAT('https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet-root/partners/edit/', CAST(fdr.id AS varchar)) AS link_to_driver_root,
fdr.status,
da."action" AS block_type_comment,
da.comment AS strategy,
da.created AS action_date,
da.id,
f.country,
ub.*,
CASE WHEN ub.created IS NOT NULL THEN row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST(ub.entity_id AS varchar)||':'||cast(da.id AS varchar) ORDER BY ub.created ASC) ELSE 0 END AS rn
FROM ng_public.fraud_action_driver_action as da
  LEFT JOIN (
      		SELECT 
      		CAST(json_extract_scalar(fci.input, '$.data.driverId') AS bigint) AS driverid,
      		json_extract_scalar(fci.input, '$.data.country') AS country,
      		fci.created_date,
      		row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST(json_extract_scalar(fci.input, '$.data.driverId') AS bigint) ORDER BY fci.created DESC) AS rownumber 
      		FROM glue.ng_fraud.driver_statistics_check_input as fci 
      		WHERE json_extract_scalar(fci.input, '$.data.country') IS NOT NULL
      		AND fci.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -6, current_date) as date)
      		)AS f ON f.driverid = da.driver_id AND rownumber = 1 
  LEFT JOIN ng_public.fleet_driver AS fd ON fd.id = da.driver_id
  LEFT JOIN ng_public.fleet_driver_root AS fdr ON fd.driver_root_id = fdr.id
  LEFT JOIN 
  			(
  			SELECT 
			al.created,
			al.id AS unblock_id,
			al.entity_id,
			al.entity_type,
			li.old_value,
			li.value,
			al."role",
			al.role_id,
			--b.first_name||'_'||b.last_name AS persona,
			CASE WHEN b.email IN ('karl.kutsar@bolt.eu', 'mari.hiie@bolt.eu', 'caroline.kruberg@bolt.eu', 'lise.vaher@bolt.eu','mariia.patrakova@bolt.eu', 'nigar.alizada@bolt.eu', 'martin.farmakov@bolt.eu','leyla.hasanova@bolt.eu') THEN 'fraud' ELSE 'not fraud' END AS unblock_group,
			b.email
			FROM ng_public.audit_log_audit_log al
			LEFT JOIN ng_pii.audit_log_log_item li ON li.log_id = al.id AND date(li.created) = date(al.created)
			LEFT JOIN ng_public.admin_admin_user b ON al."role" ='admin' AND al.role_id = b.id 
			WHERE al.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -6, current_date) as date)
			AND al."action" = 'edit'
			AND li.KEY = 'status'
			AND li.old_value = 'blocked'
			AND li.value <> 'blocked'
			AND al.entity_type = 'driver_root'
  			) AS ub ON ub.entity_id = fdr.id AND date(ub.created) >= date(da.created)
  WHERE da.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -6, current_date) as date)
      AND da.status = 'success'
      AND da.ACTION = 'fleet_hard_block_driver'
      --AND da.driver_id = 6590702
      ORDER BY da.created DESC
      --LIMIT 1000
) AS y 
WHERE y.rn <= 1
--AND y.value IS NOT NULL
--AND y.unblock_group = 'not fraud'
GROUP BY 1,2
--ORDER BY 4 DESC
--LIMIT 1000

Hey team! Adding perspective from the Risk team on the feature-

Overall, the feature was requested for Dubai (partner market), where they collaborate with DTC in order to get more rides on the platform. Doing this for a principal market (not the safest market either, where drivers are prone to scamming passengers) puts Bolt in a very uncertain position. 

*Risks:* 

*Driver Safety*: 

* Drivers are at greater risk when picking up passengers without app verification, who may have malicious intentions.

*Passenger Safety*: 

* There is no way for the passenger to contact Bolt in case an unsafe incident occurs during the trip.
* There is nothing we can do to help the passenger if we cannot find the trip on the platform 
* It is unclear how safety support (and any support) will look like if a passenger has an issue. Using the email for safety support is also a Privacy risk. 
* Privacy concern: if a passenger requests a refund, the only way to refund them is if a passenger shares their bank details with Bolt. 

*Additionally:* 

* It is unclear how Crisis Management and mitigation process will work for such cases. 

*Safety features will be unavailable* to both driver and passenger:

* Rider/Driver Emergency Assist 
* Rider/Driver Trip Sharing 
* Driver/Rider Rating
* Trip Anomaly v2 
* Driver Tickets from Ratings 
* Rider/Driver Unmatching 
* Hide Rider Address from Drivers

Hope this helps 🙏

Hey [~accountid:5cfa1447a1d0930f39e18c87], thank you for raising this request.

Under our current [General T&Cs|https://bolt.eu/en-ua/legal/tnc-delivery-partners/?category=delivery] for Partners, “…_Bolt may charge the Partner a fee for running a marketing campaign_ *_which shall be agreed between the Parties_*_._“ (clause 6.3). 

Further, under our Special Terms, “_The Special Terms of the Agreement may be amended_ *_by the parties’ agreement_* _in a form reproducible in writing_.“

The general contract rules in Ukraine according to the Civil Code (article 642) are such, that when Bolt sends an offer to the Partner to enter into any agreement (and this would be qualified as such offer since we propose to carry out some campaign that would impose financial obligations on the Partner), the acceptance of such terms *must be full and unconditional.* Silence of the partner cannot be interpreted as a positive response. Therefore, our offer without a direct positive response of the partner is not binding on the partner.

This together with our above mentioned provisions of the T&Cs means that if we do not have a full and unconditional acceptance by such terms by the partner - meaning the positive response in writing (incl. email) that cannot be interpreted in another way - we cannot impose such conditions on the partner. If we do, they can dispute it and there is a high chance that they would be successful in such dispute. 

In order to allow us to conduct such campaigns by only notifying a partner, we would need to conduct an additional analysis to determine if this can be in line with the legislation and in any case, we would need to amend at least the special terms to include such an option. Please let me know if you want to proceed with this, but this will take an additional time.

Let me know if you have any questions.

Version 1.0 is finalized.
Folder containing the workflows [here|https://bolt.workflows.okta.com/app/folders/01JJRGYGS6FDX2J6KV6DVRSJEM/flows]

* 1.0 Flow is triggered by an EventHook executed at the Campaigns End
** 2.0 Handles Pagination
*** 3.0 Writes the data into the table [here|https://bolt.workflows.okta.com/app/tables/ee87cefd-e16e-4706-aa20-2c1e6a2d90fb]
*** Once pagination finishes, the table is exported as csv and pushed to Google Drive
*** The table will be cleared and ready for the next campaign
** If the data table is not empty, the flow stops and sends a slack message to handle the reporting/backup manually. 
*** The workflow has to clear the table before it ends, which indicates that the workflow has successfully completed. If the data still exists in the table, then it either means that an ongoing workflow is active or theres been an error during the previous flow.
* Flow which name is starting with “Manual Trigger” is left in the folder to be used in case the automation fails and no report has been generated to the Drive.
** This uses a separate Table as well, so it does not infringe with the main flow.
** All in all, mostly the same flow, just needs input for Campaign ID, which is also in the Slack message

All files are uploaded to [Drive|https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0ANRhB8vhBdYqUk9PVA].

The Privacy Team has completed the analysis of the ‘ContentStudio’ platform and the Data Processing Agreement provided to us. Our recommendation is not to proceed with the conclusion of this Partnership due to the following reasons:

*Key Concerns*:

* *Partner’s responsibility*: The Agreement is being executed between our Georgian Partner, Smartly Ltd., and ContentStudio. To our knowledge, the Georgian Partner independently manages customer service-related matters without our direct involvement. As a result, while the decision to enter into this partnership and execute the Agreement rests solely with them, any potential data breaches or security incidents arising from their operations could have serious consequences for us. Such breaches may not only expose us to reputational harm but also create potential legal and financial liabilities. Additionally, the outdated 2016 Partnership Agreement and lack of data-sharing agreements in place result in a failure to clearly delineate obligations, increasing the risk of joint liability for data breaches or non-compliance.
* *Deficient DPA*: Given these considerations, the current Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is inadequate, as it fails to address several critical aspects of standard data security and applicable data-sharing requirements. This partnership involves providing Bolt with a social media management platform designed to provide customer inquiries, enable 24/7 support coverage via social media channels. As a result, substantial amounts of personal data would become accessible to the counterparty. Over the past few weeks, we’ve seen an increase in cases resolved without an issue tag in the Latvia market.

We wanted to know why and conducted a deep-dive over the last 4 weeks to see if we can identify any trends or issues agents might be struggling to identify the applicable ATI.Across last 5 weeks and 471 cases reviewed *49.89%* of cases had a suitable ATI which should’ve been added before closing the case.
Instead of presenting you all the cases reviewed, I’d like to focus on trends we identified:

# Courier ATI - I want to submit my documents
## A very large part (74 cases) of the reviewed cases were from couriers regarding FVS registrations. Even though we are not noting their FVS registration numbers, all these cases are still connected with documents the courier is required to have. Cases similar to [this|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/511115290] one, should have the ATI “I want to submit my documents” added.
# Courier lead specific ATI’s
## We noticed that this is something agents struggle with as a considerable portion of untagged cases are from Courier lead user persona. Courier lead ATI’s are quite generic and such there rarely is a case when no ATI will be applicable.
# Not always customers/users will use language that perfectly match our internal procedures/ATI. It is still up to us to determine what the actual ticket issue was.
## For example, there are many ways the customer can express that his food tasted off and didn’t meet their expectations. Mentioning that [old oil |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/526558976]was used to prepare their food is one of them.

We would like to suggest that agents go over KB articles for various user persona issues list and pay close attention to the description of the issue titles. Sometimes the issue title itself might give the impression that the ATI is not applicable but the description clears up that it is.A good example for this is provider ATI “I want to change my location”. From just the title alone, we could assume that it only applies to changes in address and location, but if we read the description (_Provider requests for their location to be changed, e.g., edit pin, add_ *_pick-up notes to couriers_*) we see that courier pick-up notes are also included.Below you can find all issue lists for delivery user personas

* [Courier Lead issues list|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360020878400?country=global&language=en]

*“How is “Home City” defined on user Admin profile”:*

* The dominant city is computed as the city with the most orders.

{noformat}------------ AGGREGATES ------------------
SELECT 
--CASE WHEN x.is_canceled = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS block_was_removed_early,
--x.unblocking_group,
x.country_code,
approx_distinct(x.blockid,0.0041) AS count_blocks
FROM (      
SELECT
da.driver_id AS driver_id,
da."action" AS block_type_comment,
da.comment AS strategy,
da.created AS action_date,
da.finish_time,
da.id,
CAST(REPLACE(da.apply_comment, 'Blocking id: ', '') AS bigint) AS blockid,
bb.*,
s.*
  FROM ng_public.fraud_action_driver_action as da
  JOIN ng_public.block_block bb ON 
 			bb.id = CAST(REPLACE(da.apply_comment, 'Blocking id: ', '') AS bigint)
 			AND bb.entity_id = da.driver_id 
 			AND bb.entity_type = 'driver'
 			AND bb.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -6, current_date) as date)
 LEFT JOIN (
 		SELECT 
 		bal.block_id,
 		bal.type,
 		bal.role_id,
 		bal."role",
 		bal.created,
 		CASE WHEN b.email IN ('karl.kutsar@bolt.eu', 'mari.hiie@bolt.eu', 'caroline.kruberg@bolt.eu', 'lise.vaher@bolt.eu','mariia.patrakova@bolt.eu', 'nigar.alizada@bolt.eu', 'martin.farmakov@bolt.eu','leyla.hasanova@bolt.eu','guilherme.franciulli@bolt.eu') THEN 'fraud' ELSE 'not fraud'END AS unblocking_group,
 		b.email 
 		FROM ng_public.block_audit_log bal
 		LEFT JOIN ng_public.admin_admin_user b ON bal."role" ='admin' AND bal.role_id = b.id
 		WHERE 
 		 bal."TYPE" = 'canceling'
 		AND bal.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -6, current_date) as date)
 )
 AS s ON s.block_id = bb.id AND bb.is_canceled = TRUE
  WHERE da.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -6, current_date) as date)
      AND da.status = 'success'
      AND da.ACTION = 'fleet_block_driver'
)AS x 
WHERE x.is_canceled = TRUE
--WHERE x.status <> 'active'
AND x.unblocking_group = 'not fraud'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC     {noformat}

+*BACKGROUND*+

* We are planning on running a campaign for drivers as part of Ramadan. This involves sending a gift (a box of dates) to 550 Dutch drivers, done via a third-party distributor.
** At the start of Ramadan, drivers will receive an email informing them about the campaign.
** Drivers are given the option to sign-up to the campaign via email.
** ‘Winners’ not determined based on performance. They are awarded on a first come, first served basis. This will be clearly [communicated|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kKDL8GUr53sIf6UhpKfLNef7b2F3rsieBMbjkkGkG6w/edit?tab=t.g6gpy1kaz7d6#heading=h.kgmnrfeu277z] up front.
*** Currently says “To deliver the gift to your doorstep we’ll need to share your address with our trusted delivery partner. By reserving a date box, you *agree to share your details with them for this purpose only*.”
** Once the ‘winners’ are selected, the dates will be shipped to the drivers' registered addresses via a third-party distribution partner.

+*REQUEST*+

* Re sharing driver addresses with third-party distributor:
** Since we need to provide Driver addresses to the third party for delivery, how should we approach consent?
** Would it be sufficient to include a clear consent statement in the campaign sign-up process, stating that by signing up, they agree to share their address with the distribution partner for this specific purpose?
*** [NB. Dawit has advised ”_By signing up for the xyz campaign, you consent to share your personal data, including your address, with our selected third-party distributor for the sole purpose of delivering the gift box of dates_”]
* -Reclassification risk-
** -Given that we are shipping the dates to Drivers' registered addresses, does this pose a reclassification risk?-
** -While we believe this is a goodwill gesture and not tied to any performance requirements, we want to ensure this does not create unintended legal risks.-

+*ANALYSIS*+

* *Risk profile*: Low.
* *Legal basis:*
** (a) Sending the comms in the first place.
*** I doubt this will result in any consent concerns, so legitimate interest should be fine.
** (b) Sharing driver’s address with third-party service provider.
*** Contractual necessity would not apply here, as no contract is in place.
*** Consent:
**** We generally avoid relying on consent unless absolutely necessary, as consent can be withdrawn. We would need to flag to the drivers their right to withdraw consent.
**** However, we need to rely on consent where we intend to share someone’s data in an unexpected or potentially intrusive way. Sharing their home address with a third party could meet this threshold. 
**** Also, if a person explicitly said they did not want us to share their home address with the third party, then we would have no other legal basis / good reason for doing so - they would simply just not be included among the ‘winners’ for the campaign. This seems compatible with consent as a legal basis.
**** Additionally, I think it is unlikely that we currently have a DPA in place with the distributor. If we do not, another de-risking factor would be to rely on the fact that the driver has still explicitly consented to us sharing their home address.
**** Ordinarily, I would prefer to rely on legitimate interest here. However, because this involves sharing home addresses with a third party, *I think we should rely on consent here*, to pre-empt any possible user complaints (sharing home addresses is the only ‘risky’ element of this campaign IMO).
*** [~accountid:712020:b2a2738f-c1f1-447c-9b72-29851b5fed3e] let me know if you disagree with this, as I appreciate that we do not ordinarily rely on consent in these circumstances. I set out my reasoning above.
* *Disclaimer*:
** I have proposed some wording on the main ticket.
** We should also advise the business that the user has the right to withdraw consent here. If they do, and we have not yet shared their details with the third party, then we should refrain from doing so.

More detailed advice / reasoning is below.

*DISCLAIMER WORDING* 

We can certainly rely on *consent* as the legal basis for sharing the drivers' addresses with the third party (indeed, this is the least risky / most transparent option from a Privacy POV). 
Before doing so, I propose the following changes:
*(1)* [+*Cover email*+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kKDL8GUr53sIf6UhpKfLNef7b2F3rsieBMbjkkGkG6w/edit?tab=t.g6gpy1kaz7d6]
We can remove “_To deliver the gift to your doorstep we’ll need to share your address with our trusted delivery partner. By reserving a date box, you agree to share your details with them for this purpose only_.” Instead, I have proposed some more detailed wording in the form.
*(2)* [+*Form*+|https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1XkmIuH0wiYhqE0yW6sFUYiDv1zg3vBywD8aeVmuH_Ew/edit]
I assume that by clicking ‘Claim a date box’ in the email, the driver is led to this form, right? I also assume that we will not be sharing this data with any other third parties?
If so, I would make the following changes:
* At the top, I would replace “_By completing and submitting this form, you consent that the data provided may be shared with third parties solely for the purpose of shipment and delivery of dates. Your data will not be used or shared for other purposes without explicit consent_” with the following wording (which covers our bases more effectively from a transparency and Privacy POV): 
{quote}“_To deliver the gift to your doorstep, we will need to share your name, email address and home address with our trusted delivery partner,_ {color:#ff5630}_[INSERT COMPANY NAME]_{color}_. By completing and submitting this form, you consent that the data provided may be shared_ _in this manner_. _Your data will not be shared for other purposes, and will be retained only as needed for this purpose. You have the right to withdraw this consent at any time. For more information on your rights and the processing of your personal data, please refer to our privacy notice available at_ [https://bolt.eu/nl-nl/privacy/privacy-policy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/nl-nl/privacy/privacy-policy-for-drivers/?category=rides] “{quote}
* Re the checkbox at the end of the form, I would replace the wording with “_I consent to the sharing of the above information with_ {color:#ff5630}_[INSERT COMPANY NAME]_ {color}_for the purpose of shipment and delivery of dates_.”
❗ *NB. Withdrawal*
If a driver provides their consent to this data sharing, they are entitled to withdraw the consent at any time. As such, if a driver provides their consent to data sharing here, but then subsequently writes to us _before_ we share it with the third party saying that they withdraw their consent, then we need to make sure we do not share their home address with the third party.

*DATA SHARING*

Given that we are sharing home addresses with this third party, we need to make sure that proper contractual protections are in place. This is to prevent:
* The third party doing what it wants with the home addresses (this could result in driver complaints issued to Bolt), including retaining this data for longer than it should; 
* The third party not taking appropriate steps to protect this information on their side; and
* Potential liabilities for Bolt if the third party does something with the home addresses that the drivers object to.
In these circumstances, we would always push for an *data processing agreement* between the parties that contains these protections. We have a standard agreement that I could quickly prepare on Monday, but before doing so, can you confirm whether such an agreement already exists? 
While it is open to the business to take a risk-based approach and proceed without such an agreement, {color:#ff5630}+*I would advise against this*+{color}, as this exposes Bolt to unnecessary risk.

From a legal standpoint, there are a few key considerations regarding rider cancellations due to CCTV in vehicles:

* *Unfair  Consumer Rights:* If a rider was +unaware of the CCTV+  before entering the vehicle, a refusal to refund the cancellation fee could be challenged under unfair commercial practices laws.
* *Data Protection:* [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] you will be a better judge of it here but as I understand, while we may not be the controller of CCTV footage, unclear notification practices could expose us to indirect risks, particularly in jurisdictions with strict privacy laws. Please elaborate in case required 🙏 
* *Operational Risks:* Frequent cancellations due to undisclosed CCTV could lead to increased refund disputes and reduced rider trust. 

h3. {color:#36b37e}In order to come to a conclusion that Bolt will not refund the cancellation fee to the rider, we need to ensure that the rider had the opportunity to opt out of a ride with CCTV before engaging with the service. {color}


To mitigate the risks above and ensure compliance, we should consider implementing a *clear disclosure requirement -* Introducing an *in-app notification* informing riders about CCTV before they confirm a trip. This I understand [~accountid:712020:2449585e-020b-4bbc-ac29-8780f94f6823] and [~accountid:712020:ae7c369e-0fb6-428c-8e40-e7775c5bbebe] are already working on. 

This would help us enforce cancellation fees while maintaining transparency and protecting against consumer rights challenges.

Hi all - as usual, sharing the main takeaways / next steps from the call earlier today:

* Captive insurance (in-house):
** Unattractive due to (1) high minimum capital requirements (at least €2.5 million in the Baltics), and (2) operational complexity (e.g., the need to register as an insurance firm + ensuring full compliance will likely require ~5+ additional FTEs).
** [@daniels.martuzans|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U081Q23BL3S] to research the (1) total MTPL-related savings potential, and (2) detailed capital requirements.
* Cutting out insurance brokers:
** ~€127k opportunity size in the Baltics + DE (+0.2% GM improvement for 1P), assuming no changes in premiums. It's TBD if we'll be able to achieve the same premiums as we do with brokers, as brokers likely have better negotiating power. On LOPS side, there is no strong preference towards working with brokers.
*** Potential next steps - as an experiment, in one of the countries we could request a quote from insurance firms directly to assess if we're able to achieve equally favourable terms when compared to deals we get via brokers.
** [@daniels.martuzans|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U081Q23BL3S] to factor in extra costs of cutting out brokers (1 additional FTE) to arrive at a comprehensive opportunity size.
* Cost-offsetting by increasing the default MTPL deductible (e.g., if user causes damages to the 3rd party, we get the right to claim a fee up to the deductible threshold; the deductible remains EUR 0 if user opts in for a paid extended protection).
** Scenario dismissed due to potentially poor customer perception & PR effect from making drives "riskier" for the user + no competitor does it.
* Cost-offsetting by reducing customer liability (related to damages caused to the vehicle) in exchange for an optional expanded protection fee.
** High-potential scenario, but it goes beyond the scope of the MTPL project => [@daniels.martuzans|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U081Q23BL3S] to discuss internally next week how & if we want to assess it.

[Courier earnings query|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5908825129/2025+Q1+TIDB+Migration+Analysis+Review+by+DBRE#Courier-Earnings-Query]
Only single slow query recorded in 3 days for a query accessed through endpoing with ~2rps. Looks more like a fluke to me and probably can be ignored. As alternative - split one query into several with fixed timeframe limit, but I don’t think we really need to.

[Tasks waiting dependencies|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5908825129/2025+Q1+TIDB+Migration+Analysis+Review+by+DBRE#Tasks-waiting-dependencies]
[PR by Rafael|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/126809] - remove NULL check (field is not nullable), remove sort by {{created}} (field not indexed, thus sorting performing slow)

[Removing old tasks|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5908825129/2025+Q1+TIDB+Migration+Analysis+Review+by+DBRE#Tasks-ordered-by-Id]
Explicit index usage can be added, however I’m thinking about options to rewrite the query, need bit more research on execution plans in TiDB. Rafael added a [PR|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/126977] with {{created}} -based query, however I have concerns about its ability to perform significantly better then setting index in query. 

[Records to export|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5908825129/2025+Q1+TIDB+Migration+Analysis+Review+by+DBRE#Records-to-Export]
The query plan provided looks really weird to me - it shows 4.3M rows under index of state + timestamp, but we don’t have that many records. At moment I checked there were about 30-40k records in {{to_export}} state and within 2 digits amount fitting the time range. As far as I see in [metrics|https://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/kxFgnLQ7z/billing-service?orgId=1&refresh=1m&var-project=delivery-invoicing-handler&from=now-90d&to=now&viewPanel=12] the flow of records is more or less constant and doesn’t have bursts that might explain pile up of 4.3M unexported records, which would require about a week of downtime. My thoughts are that either there is a TiDB setup issue and updates were not propagated properly, or we have to overhaul whore record export flow if there actually can be a case of millions of records being passed for exporting.

[Organic events processing|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5908825129/2025+Q1+TIDB+Migration+Analysis+Review+by+DBRE#Organic-Event-Processing]
We can update index from {{state}} to {{state,ignore_until}} but same as query before, for me it looks more like TiDB updates propagation misconfiguration, as at any given time amount of unprocessed events that fits the condition is within 3 digits usually. Also same queries working fine with other verticals.

[Tasks to execute|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5908825129/2025+Q1+TIDB+Migration+Analysis+Review+by+DBRE#Selecting-tasks-ready-to-execute]
[Draft PR|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/127892/files] - removed NULL condition as {{ignore_until}} field is not nullable

[Unknown task query|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5908825129/2025+Q1+TIDB+Migration+Analysis+Review+by+DBRE#Unknown-Task-query]
This is metric query from [MonitorableStatusTable|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/common/billing/monitoring/MonitorableStatusTable.ts] interface. Poor performance here is rather indicator of problematic data, not query. I’d rather suggest to add new terminal task status that will indicate manually discarded tasks. However added a [PR|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/127903/files] moving query to slave DB instance.

approx_distinct(CASE WHEN z.is_canceled = TRUE THEN z.block_id END,0.0041) *1.00 / approx_distinct(z.block_id,0.0041) AS ratio_of_unblocks_after_manual_block

* As shared before, language specialists translated from scratch and proofread AI pre-translations for 5 languages.
* We did the review, and the results are very mixed.
** On average, the AI pre-translation + Human proofreading is 10% faster than pure Human work. Given the cost of the pre-translation (<$100) this is already good but not good enough

** % words that required no or very minimal edition is 38% across all languages

Other possible solutions (by chatGPT):


# *Disable Auto-Refresh on Load*

* Go to *Dashboard Settings → Refresh Interval* and set it to *“off”* by default.
* Users can manually refresh after selecting filters.

# *Hide Panels Until a Filter is Set*

* Use Grafana’s *panel visibility feature*:
** Edit a panel.
** Go to *“Panel Options” → “Visibility”*.
** Set the condition: {{"$service" != "None"}}.
** This hides the panel until a service is selected.

# *Use a Custom Default Value Like “Select a Service”*

* Go to *Dashboard Settings → Variables* and set a custom default value like {{"Please select a service"}}.
* Update your queries to check for this and *return no data* until a valid selection is made.

# *Use “All” or “None” as the Default Variable Value*

* Create a *required filter variable* (e.g., {{$service}}) and set its default value to *empty* or {{"None"}}.
* Modify your queries to *not fetch data* when {{$service}} is unset.
* Example (for PromQL):

sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=~“$service”}[5m]))

* If {{$service}} is empty, the query won’t return results, avoiding an unnecessary load.

# *Enable Query Caching*

* If using *Prometheus*, enable *query caching* ({{query_result_cache}}).
* This helps when multiple users are loading the same data.

Hi [~accountid:712020:13033e65-435c-4794-a380-e007eba7615a] - here are my briefly outlined thoughts:

||*Topic*||*Opinion*||
|Data sharing with the delivery partner - no DPA|Considering that the reporter confirmed that the set up changed and that Bolt will deliver the dates ourselves, I believe this becomes redundant. Overall, I disagree that obtaining consent for the activity would de-risk the fact that no DPA is in place.|
|Lawful basis:
(a) Sending the comms in the first place.|I agree that this does not necessitate consent, and LI will suffice. Ideally, we need to have the LIA documented but I realise that this can be too much effort for such a low value project.|
|Lawful basis:
 (b) Sharing driver’s address with third-party service provider.|Given the recent changes to our setup, I believe we no longer require a lawful basis to share data with third parties. I suggest we rephrase the overall purpose to something like “facilitation of delivery” or a similar term.
While I agree that consent could serve as a potential lawful basis, I see it as potentially problematic. For instance, if consent is granted and the delivery is prepared, but the driver later withdraws consent, this could create unnecessary complications.
I recommend that we rely on Legitimate Interest (LI) in this case. The disclaimer can be updated accordingly. Possible LI can be fostering goodwill and driver engagement by sending gifts. I also believe that the activity and the purposes of “sending the comms in the first place” and subsequent “facilitation of delivery” can be bundled as a single activity with a single purpose under 1 lawful basis (LI).|

*On a wider note:* I am surprised to learn that our teams know the drivers religion (muslim) to offer them gifts. I do not recall us collecting this information from the drivers explicitly. Are you aware of this? If not, I suggest to dig deeper into this, as this sounds very concerning to me.

 _(b) Sharing driver’s address with third-party service provider._|_Given the recent changes to our setup, I believe we no longer require a lawful basis to share data with third parties. I suggest we rephrase the overall purpose to something like “facilitation of delivery” or a similar term._

Hi [~accountid:626bc237bae0c1006fadfd63] , thanks for the clarification!

*Some key points from me:*

* Under data protection law, personal data should only be retained if there is a clear legal, regulatory, or operational need to keep it.
* If Viber messages are not actively required for operations or compliance, retaining this data will pose unnecessary data protection risks (as we’d be keeping data that we don’t need).
* If a regulatory body (e.g., Tax Office) requires past records of changes made to driver profiles, the primary source should be official company systems (Admin, Beehive) rather than Viber messages. If certain critical historical data (such as profile changes) is not available in official systems but is stored in Viber, we it’s advised to extract the data from Viber and upload it to Admin/other systems where this data is usually kept.



*So, to sum up:*

* If we know that we’ll need this data for tax purposes (e.g. in case we receive a request from the Tax office), I suggest backing up the data and uploading it to the same system where we’re uploading the new data now. I suppose that’s admin.
* From a privacy POV, there is no difference where we upload it, but I’d advise to upload the data to our usual systems, to maintain consistency.
* I suggest backing up only the data that we need, and not everything.

Second detail is that when making the refund this can potentially be added as a negative debt to involved driver’s account. So in case they attempt to come back to the platform, they would be charged for the amount. 

As I mentioned about given this is a postpaid account fraud is not involved in large scale but we can work with business team and of course with pricing team to help creating automation for the similar cases. This will require extensive analysis before implementation given we need to make sure not to affect any good users. 

I hope this helps and feel free to reach out to me for follow up questions.

card_country,
card_issuer,
payment_provider,
count(distinct payment_order_id) as payment_orders_count,
count(distinct case when error_code=327 and error_message='PAYMENT_ERROR_FRAUD' and raw_response_orchestrator ='card.possible-fraud' then payment_order_id end) as count_fraud_decline_payment_orders,
(1.000*(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN error_code=327 and error_message='PAYMENT_ERROR_FRAUD' and raw_response_orchestrator ='card.possible-fraud' THEN payment_order_id END))/(1.000*COUNT(DISTINCT payment_order_id))) * 100.0 AS fraud_delcine_payment_ratio,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN lower(card_country) <> lower(country_code) THEN payment_order_id END) AS count_foreign_cards,
(1.000 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN lower(card_country) <> lower(country_code) THEN payment_order_id END)) / (1.000 * COUNT(DISTINCT payment_order_id)) * 100.0 AS foreign_card_ratio
FROM 
ng_commerce.payments_etl
WHERE created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -6, current_date) as date)
group by 1,2,3
having count(distinct payment_order_id)>100
order by 6 desc{noformat}

So with [~accountid:712020:902d65c1-f6d8-4b16-8d42-efa2808ca034] we ran the models.

And we did the following checks:



* *“Business” check*

We tried to understand what changes we would have as a result of the alternative scenario 

So what we did was: “Calibration + Calibrated Priors” => “No calibration and imputing experiments directly”

Results of this run are stored in [[Run Output] Normal|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LPRFqlEHzdUBVfnuimOqZQO9VOYbxilO7NNDW94cjss/edit?gid=558878217#gid=558878217] tab.

If we ran Q4 models by the new algorithm, we would get almost similar vmaxes (~10% bigger)

* *Big “Technical” check*

We tried to run the models the same way like in “business“ check, but for experiments we imputed experiment results multiplied by 10.

And these results expectedly showed massive increase of channels that were marked as having experiments

Results of this run are available in [[RUN OUTPUT] Crazy experiments|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LPRFqlEHzdUBVfnuimOqZQO9VOYbxilO7NNDW94cjss/edit?gid=558878217#gid=558878217] tab.

This check makes sure that model behaves in a correct way, increasing the coefficients of required channels (the ones that had experiment) in the correct direction (in this case, increased them)

* *Smaller “Technical“ check*

Additionally we wanted to check if adding the experiments to the models would increase or decrease vmax in the correct direction (i.e. being more aligned to experiment), but if the experiment deltas were not “crazily” big. 

For this check, 

* we took the models for Q4 with uninformed priors (we took Q3 posterior, but with No calibration).
* we added experimental data to them. 

We expected that adding the experiment would align the posterior vmax to experimental results.

And this was checked in column AG in Stats tab in this [spreadsheet|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nnC5VvwvdnNyDl6tPKxU8j-SbMshlXytsuSKBVPWgZM/edit?gid=1182665612#gid=1182665612].

*Output here is that:* In all cases (only two exceptions) models with experiments were closer to experimental results than models without experiments

(The output sounds really trivial, but this is a technical check to make sure that implementation works properly and expected)



*Also note:*

We made similar *technical* checks in this [task|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/MARTECH-6171], but here we are checking that implementation to production was done correctly.
